tests.name: Every activity has source pages, concrete frames, explanation and transfer questions
Every source-guided condition is achievable and all measured values are finite
Elementary balance changes distance as well as weight
Same movement can require a larger push or pull for a heavier load
Digital objects have distinct similar weights and cannot be read before zeroing
Spring scale readings are within capacity and on 5 g divisions
A scale trial requires the student reading; incorrect attempts and bag tare remain inspectable
Elementary lever and ramp comparisons preserve load and reference lift
Spring graph uses extension and supports a 25 cm prediction
Friction investigation starts from rest and independently varies surface and load
Air, one submerged weight, two submerged weights give correct buoyancy differences
Diver volume, balloon payload and submarine ballast are different causal controls
Exact high-school three-row lever experiment balances in each row
A couple can have zero resultant and nonzero torque
Tilted structures use the support edge, centre height and base width together
A 3 m shelf with 120 N at 2 m gives 40 N wall support and 80 N tension
Drawing assessment checks body, magnitude and direction rather than answer clicks
Completion requires actual measurements, answers, explanation, prediction and reflection
Old v1 records are preserved as earlier evidence; new guided completion is not invented
Earlier v2 cart, ornament and wrench records migrate without inventing resultant-review trials
Export/import keeps predictions, first and corrected answers, plans and separated school records
